title: feat(post): Tormach PathPilot post and 770MX machine; machine units reach posts
body:
## What changed

Adds Tormach support for #131: a **Tormach PathPilot** post and a **Tormach 770MX** machine. This first PR is 3-axis only. The contributor's own MicroArc 4th axis is left for a follow-up.

### The post, `assets/posts/tormach.cps` (registry name `Tormach PathPilot`)
It's built on `haas.cps`'s structure, with the PathPilot/LinuxCNC rules from Tormach's and LinuxCNC's public documentation (sources are in the file's provenance header):
- **Program framing:**
  - No `%` fence, as Tormach's post guidelines ask, and no `O` program number, because LinuxCNC reads an O word as a subroutine label.
  - The program opens with a `( )` name comment and ends with `M30`.
- **Header:**
  - The modal state: `G20`/`G21`, `G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G49 G80`. Incremental arc centers are stated explicitly rather than assumed.
  - Path blending on its own line, `G64 P0.001` (in) or `P0.025` (mm). A bare `G64` means no tolerance at all in plain LinuxCNC.
- **Units come from the machine:** an inch `.mch` posts `G20`, with every length divided by 25.4 at 4 decimals and every feed divided by 25.4 at 2 decimals. A metric machine posts `G21` and mm, as before.
- **Tool changes:**
  - `G53 G0 Z0`, then `G30`, before every `T.. M6`. Tormach recommends the G30, and none of its documentation says M6 moves to a safe position by itself. A bare G30 can move X, Y and Z together, so Z goes straight up first, the same Z-first order PathPilot's own programs use between tools.
  - Then `G43 H..`, which picks up the length the tool table holds (measured by the electronic tool setter).
  - Tool numbers outside PathPilot's 1–1000 table are refused by name.
  - **X/Y first:** X and Y are unknown at program start and after every G30. So the first move after a tool change is preceded by `G0 X.. Y..` alone, at the Z-up height (a rapid's target, a feed or arc's start point, or a cycle's first hole), and only then does Z come down. This is PathPilot's own XY-first order. Then, for a first move that is a feed (a face plunges from its clearance start), it rapids Z down to the stream's start height, so the feed runs only the planned stretch instead of the whole stroke from the top of Z at the plunge rate (85baabe). It was found by the PathPilot Hub v2.14.4 simulator, which warned: "Axis XY not specified by this or previous motions, end point will depend on current position".
- **Belt range:** the 770 family has a manual belt (low 175–3250 rpm, high 525–10000 rpm) and no G or M code can change it. When a speed fits only one range, the program says which in a comment before the spindle starts.
- **Canned cycles:**
  - G73, G81, G82, G83, G86 and G89, with G98.
  - Dwell `P` in **seconds**, as LinuxCNC reads it; Fanuc-family controls read milliseconds.
  - `G84` tapping with no P: Tormach documents G84 for PathPilot, PathPilot sizes the bottom dwell itself, and the MX mills tap from the spindle encoder.
- **Program end:** `G53 G0 Z0`, `G30`, `M30`. Z goes straight up to the top of travel in machine coordinates, then the machine moves to the operator's preset G30 location. That is the order PathPilot's own Conversational programs end in.
- **Refused by name, like the other non-Fanuc posts:** cutter compensation in the control, and tilted (RTCP) moves.

### The machine, `assets/machines/tormach-770mx.mch` (library entry `Tormach 770MX`)
- **Values:** all in inches, from Tormach's "UM10587: 770MX Operator's Manual" (0626A), §2.1–2.2:
  - travel X 14, Y 7.5, Z 13.25 in, stated as bands in **program coordinates**, the full stroke each way (X ±14, Y ±7.5, Z ±13.25 in). The machine check reads travel relative to the work offset, and where G54 sits is the operator's choice. A machine-style band (Z −13.25..0) blocked every clearance move above G54 Z0; the first real GUI job refused to post that way. Fixed in b189c96 and pinned by `tormach_post::a_face_job_on_the_built_in_770mx_passes_the_gate_and_posts_inch`;
  - spindle 175–10000 rpm, 1.1 kW;
  - 300 ipm on X and Y, 250 ipm on Z;
  - a 10-tool ATC;
  - Flood M8 and Mist M7.
- **Not stated:** the spindle body size and tool-length limits. Tormach doesn't publish them, so the machine check doesn't test against them.

### Small core change: the machine's units reach the post
`.mch` files could already be in inches, but the parser scaled everything to mm and dropped the unit, so a post couldn't tell an inch machine from a metric one.
- `Machine` gains `units: Option<String>`: `Some("inch")` when the file states inches. It's skipped when `None`, so project files don't change.
- The post mirror and `script_props` expose it as `machine.units` (`"inch"` or `"mm"`), the prelude defaults it to `"mm"`, and `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` documents it.
- The other shipped posts ignore the field, so their goldens don't move.

## Readings

- **Suites that pass:**
  - `conformance` (6, with the new `nc/tormach/` goldens)
  - `tormach_post` (7, new)
  - `machine` (32)
  - `posting` (17)
  - `fanuc_post` (8)
  - `control_comp` (4)
  - `arc_planes` (8)
  - `vertical_arc_entry` (3)
  - `camcraft-post` (all)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets`: clean.
- `scripting` (17): `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` is regenerated for the post-name list.
- **Failing, but also failing on `main` without this PR:**
  - `lathe_post::facing_posts_to_the_lathe_golden` (the posted program now carries verify warnings)
  - 3 tests each in `turning_bore` and `turning_contour`, all reporting `RapidInStock`
  - the two cross-drill tests in #151
  - on this Mac, the three headless-GPU UI tests (no fallback graphics adapter)
- **PathPilot Hub v2.14.4 (simulator):** all five samples load.
  - `01-face`: its X/Y warning is fixed by 9cb46a6. A "Y exceeds machine maximum" warning came from where the simulator's G54 sat, not from the post.
  - `02-contour`, `03-pocket`, `04-peck-drill`: clean.
  - `05-tap`: `G84` is accepted, but the simulator stops every rigid tap with "Spindle reversal exceeded maximum overshoot". It stops at a constant ~9 spindle turns at both 300 and 800 rpm, with the simulated spindle not running, so this is the simulator's limit; the real machine (below) taps clean.
- **Real Tormach 770MX (contributor's machine), air cuts, PathPilot 2.14.4:**
  - `01-face`, `02-contour`, `03-pocket`, `04-peck-drill`: run to the end, including the real ATC tool changes (Z up, `G30`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, X/Y first) and the `G73` peck.
  - `05-tap` (`G84`, 600 rpm, `F15`, high belt): runs to the end with no overshoot error, so rigid tapping works as posted.
  - Its "Program exceeds machine maximum on Z" warnings came from where G54 Z and the tool length sat in the air-cut setup, and cleared as G54 Z was lowered.
  - `05b-tap-300rpm` (low belt only): PathPilot refused S300 in the high range, then timed out reaching 300 rpm when the range setting didn't match the belt's pulley position. That's an operator setup step, and it's exactly what the post's "NEEDS THE LOW BELT RANGE" comment flags.
- **First real job (GUI → post → 770MX):** Face + 2D Contour, G54 Z0 on the stock top, T31 measured by the tool setter. It ran correctly with two hand edits to the posted file: T/H renumbered to 31 (#221), and a rapid to clearance before the face's first feed (now done by the post, 85baabe).
- **Known limit (separate issue #221):** CamCraft has no per-tool number, so `T`/`H` are the tool's position in the document's tool list. For ATC jobs, keep the document's tool order the same as the PathPilot tool table until #221 lands.

## Pinning tests

- `tormach_post::the_machine_file_states_inches_and_the_script_sees_them`
- `tormach_post::a_pathpilot_program_has_no_fence_and_no_o_or_n_words`
- `tormach_post::an_inch_machine_posts_every_length_and_feed_in_inches`
- `tormach_post::a_dwell_posts_in_seconds`
- `tormach_post::a_tap_posts_g84_with_its_feed_and_no_dwell_word`
- `tormach_post::the_belt_range_is_named_and_a_stray_tool_number_is_refused`
- `tormach_post::the_registry_ships_the_tormach_post_for_mills`
- `tormach_post::every_tool_change_lifts_z_before_g30` (two tools)
- `tormach_post::the_first_move_after_a_tool_change_positions_xy_with_z_up`
- `conformance::every_builtin_posts_every_golden_byte_exact` (new `nc/tormach/` goldens) and `every_builtin_declares_its_controls_file_extension`
- `machine::every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration` (the new library entry)
- The Tormach post joins the existing refusal tests: `non_rtcp_dialects_refuse_a_tilted_stream`, and the two control-compensation refusal tests in `control_comp` and `crates/post/tests/comp.rs`.

## Notes for review

- **Checked against PathPilot's own output:** the contributor shared programs written by PathPilot Conversational: rectangular and spiral facing (2.12), and circular drilling and external thread milling (2.14.4), all with defaults and in inch. They were used to check behaviour only; no text was copied. The post matches them on:
  - no `%` and no O word;
  - `G20` and `G17 G90`;
  - Z lifted before the `G30` that precedes `T.. M6`, then `G43 H..`;
  - drilling: `G98`, `G81` and `G83 … Q`, bare X Y lines for the following holes, and `G80`;
  - `M9`/`M5`, then ending at the G30 preset, then `M30`.

  Where it differs, on purpose:
  - **Blending:** PathPilot's default is `G64 P0.005 Q0`. This post writes `G64 P0.001`, a tighter tolerance for CAM finishing paths, so it is a little slower at corners and easy to loosen if hardware tests say so.
  - **Order and layout:** coolant and spindle come in the other order, and T/M6/G43 sit on separate lines. Both are equivalent to the controller.

- **Specs from the manual:** the 770MX operator's manual settles two figures the web pages disagreed on: 250 ipm on Z, and belt ranges of 175–3250 / 525–10000 rpm.
- **The dialect checked against the manual:** chapter 10 (G-codes, canned cycles, M-codes) and the G30 sections confirm what the post writes: dwell P in seconds, `G91.1` as the default arc mode, `G64 P~ Q~`, `G84` with an optional P (the manual's own example has none), a G30 right before tool changes, and `Txx M06` loading from the ATC or pausing for a manual change. The post's provenance header cites the manual.
- **G84 on non-MX machines:** non-MX 770s (R8 spindle) may not rigid-tap. Telling those machines apart needs a capability flag in the machine file, which is a possible follow-up.
- **`post` CLI:** given a checker-layout `.mch` (like `vmc.mch` or this file), the CLI reads the units but not the machine name or coolant codes. That limitation already exists for `vmc.mch`; the app path (`posting::machine_value`, parser then mirror) reads all three.

Changelog: New Tormach PathPilot post and Tormach 770MX machine; a machine file in inches now posts inch (G20) programs through posts that read `machine.units`

Refs #131. Partial on purpose: the issue stays open until the contributor's PathPilot Hub and on-machine checks report back, and for the MicroArc 4th axis.
